findings.summary: 'What changed (library round 25)': 'for inputs and values that are zero or normal these are the old magnitudes' is wrong for p16L and ds16L; the Figures bullet omits the HEAD_DIM = 128 changes
findings.detail: (1) README, What changed (library round 25), after the Specification bullets: 'For inputs and values that are zero or normal these are the old magnitudes.' This holds for lm (aQK, aVD, lm dO, lm Q, lm K). It does not hold for p16L = lift16 p16B and ds16L = lift16 ds16B. These are functions of the bound, not of the float16 value. They differ from the old p16B, ds16B whenever the bound is below 2^-14, whatever the value: 2^-14 when the bound is in [2^-24, 2^-14), which includes pairs whose float16 P or dS is 0; and 0 when the bound is below 2^-24. That is where the table's changes come from. The Specification section states the lift correctly ('may be a nonzero subnormal ... one certainly below 2^-24 is 0 and counts 0'). What would resolve it: say that lm is the old magnitude on zero and normal values, and that p16L, ds16L equal p16B, ds16B when the bound is at least 2^-14. (2) The Figures bullet says only the test's HEAD_DIM = 128 dVTol and 'the benchmark's HEAD_DIM = 64 figures' changed. The benchmark's HEAD_DIM = 128 row changed as well (causal dKTol 90th percentile 1.50 to 1.51%). So did the text below the table (largest causal dV ratio 0.91 to 0.92%). (3) Minor, in text unchanged since round 2: the largest dQ absolute tolerance among the worst sampled rows is 0.0092498 (benchmark, HEAD_DIM = 128, CAUSAL), so 9.2*10^-3, not 9.3*10^-3. Not blocking: Spec.lean is right, and the table matches the script.
findings.evidence: work/readme_script.out: the README's inline script, run as written (numpy 2.3.5); it matches the table. The old figures are those of my round-2 run of the previous script. work/floor.out: per-row floor figures on the benchmark's low-mass rows, and the 5-digit dQ absolute value.

release.note: Settled by L126 (library round 25). DotF16 is now forall p, DotLiftAcc P <f16, f16, f32, p, 0> relDot16 absDot16, with the same constants, relative to |acc| + sum liftMag a * liftMag b. liftMag counts a subnormal float16 operand at minNormal8 .f16 = 2^-14, which is the device mechanism I asked about. num.md lists it under 'Facts the library states', with evidence num-dot-sub16-round25. The claim is re-proved on the restated fact. The spec counts every tl.dot operand by its lifted magnitude (lm in aQK and aVD; p16L * lm dO, ds16L * lm Q, ds16L * lm K in the accumulations), so ppT, dsT and subnormal inputs stay covered.

notes: Round 3, gate b28f50727b67c8a8. Re-opened: assumption:dot, dot_total, exp2, exp2_total and spec. model, map, conditions and faithful are unchanged. assumption:dot: the field is Rules.Num.DotF16 P, the fact as listed in num.md's 'Facts the library states' (row DotF16, DotBF16, restated 2026-11-01), now a DotLiftAcc. Its docstring describes it correctly. dot_total, exp2, exp2_total: against the round-24 commit, the diffs of Num.lean, Sm90.lean and num.md leave DotTotal, Exp2F32 and MathTotal and their num.md rows unchanged; they re-opened only through the file digests. spec: the new lm (liftMag .f16 of the value) and lift16 are explicit and computable. lift16 B bounds lm x for |x| <= B, since a float16 value below 2^-24 is 0. rH and aH are still relDot16 and absDot16 at HEAD_DIM. stepRel and stepAbs (DotLoop) are unchanged. pBr, pE, p16Err and dsErr changed digest only through aQK and aVD. The README's new inline script implements these formulas, and its output matches every table figure. Each change from the old figures is at most 0.07 percentage points. The floor statement still holds: on the benchmark's low-mass rows the lift adds at most about 5e-5 (at most about 250 lifted pairs per row) to a 2^-25-per-pair floor of 3.9e-4. One DOC finding, on the change log's wording, does not block.
